Richard Shivaji Roa Holkar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
Through Food ... on 26 September, 2025

Author: Subodh Abhyankar
Bench: Subodh Abhyankar
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:28555
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Subodh Abhyankar
 On The 26th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 36383 of 2025
 Richard Shivaji Roa Holkar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Food Safety Officer
 Food And Drug Aministration Department
 Appearance:

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Avinash Sirpurkar- Senior Advocate with Shri Harsh

. 
 Shri Hemant Sharma- G.A. for the State.
ORDER Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 against the order dated 03.07.2025, whereby, the petitioner's application filed under Section 317 of Cr.P.C. for exemption from personal appearance in the Trial Court has been rejected on the ground that the judgement in the case was to be delivered and the petitioner has not marked his presence.

3] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner was granted permanent exemption on 16.05.2019, copy of which, is also filed on record,
wherein, his application for permanent exemption has been accepted, with a further direction that as and when directed, he shall appear before the Court.

Learned senior counsel has submitted that the case was fixed for delivery of judgement on 28.06.2025, on which date, an application for exemption from appearance was filed, which was accepted, however, the petitioner was directed to appear on 03.07.2025, i.e., after five days.

sentences.text: 1 4] Shri Avinash Sirpurkar, learned senior counsel for the petitioner has also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28555 2 MCRC-36383-2025 submitted that the petitioner was abroad at the time when he was required to appear in the Court, and thus, he could not mark his appearance, and he is ready to appear before the Court as and when directed.

It is submitted that only on one date,
the petitioner could not appear due to the aforesaid fact.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is a reputed person, and is the owner of the place where the restaurant was being run by the other accused persons, and a case under Section 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 has been slapped against him.
5] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.

Having considered the rival submissions, and on perusal of the record, including the proceedings dated 16.05.2019,
wherein, his application for permanent exemption has been allowed, and the fact that he was asked to appear in the Trial Court on 03.07.2025 vide its order dated 28.06.2025, and at that time, the petitioner was abroad, in such circumstances, his non-appearance in the Trial Court appears justified, and in such circumstances, the petition deserves to be allowed.
7] Accordingly, the impugned order dated 03.07.2025 is hereby set aside, and the petitioner is directed to appear in the Trial Court on 07.10.2025.
8] With the aforesaid, M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Richard Shivaji Roa Holkar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Food ... on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31337923/
